classification.difficultyReason: Construct a slope table and field, sketch dependent solution curves, and explain isoclines, concavity and an asymptote.

inlines.text: Complete the table of values for the slope field.

spec.sourceRegion: Coordinate frame to the right of the table
spec.description: Editable axes for the shared response. Source answer elements and curves are removed; source numeric labels retained. No background grid.
spec.mathematics: Equal coordinate units. Labelled x ticks -1,1,2 and y ticks -2,-1,1; table coordinates span x=-1 to 2 and y=-2 to 1 in steps of one half.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes and numeric labels visible; field and curves hidden.

inlines.text: . The completed table gives all 49 values.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Through each grid point above, draw a line element $\frac12$ cm long with gradient from the table.

answer.short: The shared graph shows the completed slope field.
answer.worked: Centre a $\frac12$ cm line element at each table coordinate with gradient $x-y$. Elements are horizontal on $y=x$, rise to the right below this line and fall to the right above it.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Look for matching entries (isoclines) in the table and check they agree with your graph.

answer.short: The isoclines are $y=x+k$, where $k$ is constant.

inlines.text: Thus entries match along these diagonals, and the corresponding line elements are parallel.

children.label: e
children.prompt: What concavity would you expect for the solution curve through the origin?

inlines.text: , so the curve is concave up there. The curve stays above the solution line
along this curve. It remains concave up.

answer.short: See the curve through $(0,0)$ in the shared graph.
answer.worked: Start at $(0,0)$ with a horizontal tangent and follow the field in both directions. The curve has a minimum at the origin and is concave up.

answer.short: See the two additional curves in the shared graph.
answer.worked: Through $(-1,-1)$, begin with gradient $-1-(-1)=0$ and follow the field to form a concave-up curve with a minimum there. Through $(1,-1)$, begin with gradient $1-(-1)=2$ and follow the field to form an increasing, concave-down curve.

children.label: h
children.prompt: Which line do all solution curves appear to have as an asymptote?

answer.worked: The sketched curves approach the line $y=x-1$ as $x$ increases.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Is this line a solution of the DE?

inlines.text: The equation is satisfied, so the line is itself a solution.

spec.description: Complete shared answer graph: all 49 slope elements and the three requested solution curves, with continuation arrows. No background grid appears in the source.
